target.title: feat(gateway): propagate approvals to ancestor sessions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sub-agent approvals currently exist only on their source runtime surfaces. Parent and orchestrator operators cannot opt into a sanitized lifecycle stream, and reconnecting clients have no authoritative pending replay.

Related to #103505. Stacked on #103912.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add an opt-in `session.approval` projection for exact source and persisted ancestor audience keys.
- Keep approval routing observational: no transcript rows, `sessions.changed` events, agent turns, or wakeups.
- Filter every live event and replay row through the approval record's reviewer authorization.
- Return a bounded, authoritative pending replay with filtered keyset scanning so hidden records cannot starve visible ones or distort `truncated`.
- Reconcile durable expiry through the owning manager and publish one terminal tombstone.
- Close the replay/live handoff gap by subscribing before the snapshot and restoring the exact prior subscription if replay setup fails.
- Generate typed Swift session-approval models and status-specific terminal reason enums from the protocol source of truth.

## User Impact

Control UI and native clients can subscribe one session stream and observe sanitized pending/terminal approval truth raised by that session or its descendants. A reconnect receives the current pending set, while first-answer-wins resolution and record-level reviewer binding remain enforced by the canonical approval service.

target.title: fix(hooks): report agent startup admission failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/hooks/agent` could return HTTP success as soon as an isolated agent run was queued, even if the run failed before reaching runner-entry/session admission. For Symphony Kanban this made a hook dispatch look durable while the worker had actually hit a lifecycle/startup failure such as:

`Session "agent:herbert-karajan:hook:symphony-kanban" changed while starting work. Retry.`

That left the board with an accepted dispatch but no reliable worker closeout path.

This PR changes agent hook dispatch so startup/admission failures surface through the HTTP response before the idempotency key is cached:

- waits for `onExecutionStarted` before returning `{ ok: true, runId }`
- returns `409` for changed/deleted/archived session startup failures
- returns `503` if runner entry does not start before the admission timeout
- returns `502` for other pre-start failures
- keeps post-start failures on the existing async/log/system-event path
- preserves hook session-key policy and `deliver:false` behavior

target.title: feat(tui): opt-in persistence and agent visibility for `!`/`!!` local shell commands
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

TUI-local `!`-prefixed shell commands render a live local echo but are never persisted: closing the TUI loses them, session resume never shows them, and the agent cannot see what the operator ran or what it printed — even though the `BashExecutionMessage`/`excludeFromContext` data model and the LLM-context filtering for it already exist in `packages/agent-core` (previously unused by any production code path).

Split out of #103147 per review feedback there; that PR now carries only the rendering fixes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Operators often run a `!` command specifically to show the agent something (Claude Code's own `!` behaves this way). But local shell output can also be sensitive, so persistence and model visibility must be a deliberate choice, not a silent default:

- The session consent prompt now offers **No** / **Yes, local only** / **Yes, and share with the agent**. **Local only is the shipped, pre-existing behavior and stays the default expectation** — nothing is saved or shared unless the operator explicitly picks the share option.
- With sharing enabled, `!cmd` persists agent-visible (the agent sees it on its next turn) and `!!cmd` persists history-only (`excludeFromContext: true`, never reaches the model). Both semantics are stated in the consent prompt itself.

Implementation: an additive, hidden (`advertise: false`, `operator.admin`) `chat.injectBashExecution` gateway RPC modeled on `chat.inject`, implemented in both TUI backends (embedded calls the shared core directly in-process; gateway goes over the RPC). No live broadcast: the originating client already rendered its own local echo. History replay renders `bashExecution` entries on session resume.

Two defects found during review/testing are fixed here as well:

- A failed spawn emits both `error` and `close`; a shared settled-guard ensures one command persists at most once.
- Rows injected while an agent run is in flight now carry `appendMode: "side"` (like `chat.inject`'s assistant bookkeeping rows) so they do not steal the run's active leaf. Without this, persisting a `!` result mid-run tripped the embedded runner's session-file fence ("session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released") and killed the run. The run adopts side entries into the chain on its next append, so the agent still sees them next turn.

## User Impact

- Default behavior is unchanged: `!` commands stay local-only unless the operator opts into sharing at the consent prompt.
- With sharing enabled, `!` output survives session resume and is visible to the agent next turn; `!!` output survives resume but never reaches the model.
- Running a shared `!` command while the agent is mid-turn no longer kills the run with a session takeover error.

## Evidence

- `src/tui/tui-local-shell.test.ts` — 12 tests: consent options (local-only default persists nothing; share option persists), `!` vs `!!` `excludeFromContext` round-trip, no-scope/no-backend skips, persistence-failure surfacing, once-only persistence on error-then-close, plus the pre-existing output-cap/UTF-16/cwd guards.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.inject-bash-execution.test.ts` — parentId chain preserved, `excludeFromContext` round-trip, **mid-run side-append regression test** (fence takeover repro), idle active-append, unresolved-identity failure.
- `src/tui/gateway-chat.test.ts`, `src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts` — both backend implementations (RPC params/result shapes; embedded in-process delegation and failure surfacing).
- `src/gateway/server-methods-list.test.ts` — hidden method not advertised, handler dispatchable.
- Full `src/tui` suite green locally; protocol schema regenerated (`pnpm protocol:gen` / `protocol:gen:swift` — Swift models committed).
- Redacted PTY evidence of live `!` vs `!!` behavior: to follow in a comment.

target.title: fix(config): reject zero-value resetArchiveRetention to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Configuring `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention: "0h"` (or any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to zero) is silently accepted by Zod config validation. `parseDurationMs("0h")` returns `0` without throwing, so the `superRefine` passes the value. `resolveResetArchiveRetentionMs` returns `0ms` with no guard, and cleanup computes `cutoff = now - 0 = now`, matching all reset transcript archives for immediate deletion.

## Changes

**Schema gate (prevention)**: Added `ms <= 0` guard in `superRefine` to reject any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to ≤ 0 at config validation time. The documented disable sentinel (`false`) is unaffected.

**Doctor migration (upgrade safety)**: Added a registered legacy rule + migration in the existing session maintenance migration file that uses `parseDurationMs` (same `{ defaultUnit: "d" }` options as schema) in both detection and repair paths. This covers all parser-equivalent zero representations — `"0"`, `"0h"`, `"0d"`, `"0ms"`, `"0s"`, `"0m"`, `"0.0h"`, `"0h0m"`, `"0h0m0s"`, etc. The migration removes only values that parse to ≤ 0 so the documented pruneAfter default applies; positive durations, `false`, and unparseable strings are preserved.

### Files changed (4 files, +248/-3)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.session.ts` | +14/-3: reject zero-duration in superRefine |
| `src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts` | +27: schema regression cases |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.ts` | +49: parser-backed rule + migration spec |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts` | +155: 16 focused tests |

## Evidence

### All tests passing

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts
Tests  13 passed (13)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts
Tests  16 passed (16)
```

### Before fix: schema gate rejects zero values

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"resetArchiveRetention":"0h"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{
  "valid": false,
  "path": "/tmp/cfg.json5",
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention",
      "message": "duration must be positive (use ms, s, m, h, d), e.g. 30d"
    }
  ]
}
```

### After fix: positive intervals still accepted

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"resetArchiveRetention":"30d"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/cfg.json5","warnings":[]}
```

### After fix: `false` (documented disable) unaffected

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"resetArchiveRetention":false}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/cfg.json5","warnings":[]}
```

### Doctor detection → repair

Doctor detects via parser-backed rule:

```
session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention is a zero duration — this
causes immediate deletion of all reset transcript archives. Run
"openclaw doctor --fix" to remove it so the documented pruneAfter
default applies.
```

Doctor repairs:

```
Removed session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention "0h" (zero duration);
documented pruneAfter default applies.
```

### Unparseable values preserved for schema diagnostic

`"abc"`, `""` — not matched by doctor rule, not removed by migration. Schema diagnostic handles these.

### Diff whitespace checks

`git diff --check` passed.

- **Not tested / proof gaps**: None.

target.title: fix(ios): block omitted share attachments
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103363.

The iOS Share Extension accepted at most three image attachments and ignored videos, files, PDFs, and unknown attachment providers while still moving toward the normal send flow. That let a user share partial content without any visible explanation.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the current gateway media contract unchanged: the share route still sends image attachments only, and it does not attempt to add video/PDF/file transport in this PR.

Instead, extraction now records selected image count, accepted image count, and unsupported attachment classes. If the extension would omit selected content, the compose card enters the existing blocked state with a concrete recovery message, so send stays disabled until the user removes omitted items and shares again.

## User Impact

- Sharing 6 images now shows: `Only 3 of 6 images can be sent. Remove omitted items and share again.`
- Sharing a video, PDF/file, or unknown attachment now shows an unsupported-item message instead of silently sending only text or the first accepted images.
- Normal shares with up to 3 images are unchanged.

```text
OpenClaw Share cannot send 1 video(s), 2 file(s), 1 unsupported item(s) yet. Remove omitted items and share again.
```

target.title: fix(plugins): keep API key preview from splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the API-key preview shown during provider setup could emit isolated UTF-16 surrogate halves when the pasted key contains astral characters (e.g., emoji).

## Why This Change Was Made

`formatApiKeyPreview` used raw `String.prototype.slice` for its head and tail snippets, which can cut through surrogate pairs. It now uses the repository's existing `sliceUtf16Safe` helper so the redacted preview always stays on valid UTF-16 boundaries. The change is limited to this display helper and its test.

## User Impact

Setup confirmation prompts and status output that display API-key previews remain well-formed when the key value contains non-BMP characters.

## Evidence

- Added regression tests in `src/plugins/provider-auth-input.test.ts` covering ASCII redaction and astral boundary cases.
- Existing provider auth input tests continue to pass.
- Fixed a test callback that passed `Array.map`'s numeric index as the formatter's `opts` argument; it now uses an explicit unary wrapper.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Before the patch, `formatApiKeyPreview("a😀b")` returned `"a\ud83d…\ude00b"` (isolated surrogate halves at both edges). After the patch it returns `"a…b"`.
- **Real environment tested:** Local checkout of `fix/provider-auth-preview-utf16` at `c5ea197606ae06c8b1dc4700c2781667360cb5b8`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { formatApiKeyPreview } from "./src/plugins/provider-auth-input.ts"; for (const v of ["a😀b", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(20), "x".repeat(20) + "😀abc", "😀".repeat(10)]) console.log(JSON.stringify(formatApiKeyPreview(v)));'
  ```

target.title: fix(browser): invalidate stale roleRefs on main-frame navigation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where browser role refs (`e1`, `e2`, …) from a snapshot taken on page A could resolve to wrong elements on page B after a main-frame navigation. Three cached fields were stale after navigation: `state.roleRefs`, `state.roleRefsMode`/`state.roleRefsFrameSelector`, and the cross-Page `roleRefsByTarget` cache.

Additionally, the v1 fix stored navigation generation per-`PageState`, but `roleRefsByTarget` is intentionally shared across replacement `Page` objects. A replacement Page starting at generation zero could restore stale pre-navigation refs or reject fresh post-navigation refs.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. **framenavigated listener** clears `roleRefs`/`roleRefsMode`/`roleRefsFrameSelector` on main-frame navigation
2. **Target-scoped navGen** (`navGenerationByTarget` map keyed by `cdpUrl+targetId`) shared across replacement Pages via `pageTargetKeys` WeakMap
3. **Eviction** of `navGenerationByTarget` entries alongside `roleRefsByTarget` eviction (prevents unbounded map growth)
4. **restore guard** compares cached navGen with current target generation

## User Impact

- Stale refs after navigation throw "Unknown ref" instead of silently clicking wrong elements
- Replacement Page objects correctly share navigation lifecycle
- No impact on subframe navigations, page close, or existing workflows

## Real behavior proof

### Real Chrome/CDP proof (Google Chrome 138 + Playwright CDP)
```
Real Chrome/CDP proof: roleRefs invalidation on navigation

[phase 1] Snapshot on Page A
  Page A loaded: file:///tmp/.../page-a.html
  ok: refLocator resolves e1 on page A

[phase 2] Navigate to Page B
  Page B loaded: file:///tmp/.../page-b.html
  ok: FIXED: refLocator throws Unknown ref after navigation (stale ref rejected)
  ok: FIXED: refLocator throws Unknown ref for e2 too

[phase 3] Fresh snapshot on Page B
  ok: fresh snapshot stores refs on Page B

[phase 4] Replacement Page (new Page for same target)
  ok: replacement Page restores refs for same target

[phase 5] Navigate back to Page A
  ok: FIXED: refs cleared after second navigation
  ok: re-snapshot after second navigation works

Environment: Google Chrome 138 + Playwright CDP
ALL REAL CHROME PROOF ASSERTIONS: 7 passed, 0 failed
```

### Negative control (per-PageState navGen reverted): 20/21

target.body:
Fixes openclaw/openclaw#104136

## What Problem This Solves

`repairIMessageConversationAnchor()` recovered conversation anchors from exact-GUID `messages.history` rows but only overlaid `chat_id` / `chat_guid` / `chat_identifier`. It preserved stale notification `sender`, `destination_caller_id`, and `is_from_me`, which could:

1. Route a direct reply at the local iMessage identity instead of the remote peer.
2. Dispatch an outgoing row as inbound when history says `is_from_me: true` but the broken notification said `false`.

## Changes

- Build a complete **authoritative recovery projection** from exact-GUID history rows (sender, direction, conversation fields).
- **Keep `destination_caller_id` optional** per imsg payload contract; when history omits it, **clear** any stale notification value.
- **Fail-closed** on incomplete/conflicting projections; **drop recovered `is_from_me: true` rows**.

target.title: fix(browser): normalize geolocation permission origins
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users calling Browser `/set/geolocation` with a normal page URL in `origin`, such as `https://x.test/path`, did not get the same origin normalization as `/permissions/grant`, and malformed or `file://` origins were not rejected before the Playwright geolocation set path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Browser routes now share one HTTP(S) origin parser. `/set/geolocation` normalizes supplied origins to `URL.origin` before invoking Playwright and rejects non-HTTP(S) or malformed origins for geolocation set operations with the same error used by the dedicated permissions route.

The clear path intentionally returns before parsing `origin`, because clearing geolocation and permissions does not use an origin. This preserves existing clients that send stale or malformed origin fields while clearing state.

## User Impact

Users can pass page URLs as geolocation permission origins and get the expected site origin grant. Invalid local-file or malformed origins fail fast with a clear 400 response for set operations instead of reaching the browser mutation path. `clear=true` still clears geolocation even when an unused origin field is malformed.

## Evidence

Exact head: `4c82a884ebec97d3d4a22b79e072fdc9697a4c76`.

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 2 files / 25 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/origin.ts` passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.storage.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/permissions.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/origin.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Proof

- The route-level `/set/geolocation` proof exercises the registered Browser route handler with the Playwright geolocation adapter mocked at the plugin boundary.
- It proves a supplied page URL, `https://geo.example/path?query=1#hash`, is normalized before the adapter call, and Playwright receives `origin: "https://geo.example"`.
- It proves `file:///tmp/page.html` and malformed set origins return 400 before tab resolution and before any Playwright geolocation call.
- It proves `clear=true` returns before parsing unused coordinates or origin, so malformed unused origin input cannot block geolocation clearing; the adapter receives `clear: true` for the selected tab.
- The sibling `/permissions/grant` route proof remains in the focused run to show the shared HTTP(S) origin parser keeps permission-origin behavior aligned.

target.title: fix(config): reject zero-value resetArchiveRetention to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Configuring `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention: "0h"` (or any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to zero) is silently accepted by Zod config validation. `parseDurationMs("0h")` returns `0` without throwing, so the `superRefine` passes the value. `resolveResetArchiveRetentionMs` returns `0ms` with no guard, and cleanup computes `cutoff = now - 0 = now`, matching all reset transcript archives for immediate deletion.

## Changes

**Schema gate (prevention)**: Added `ms <= 0` guard in `superRefine` to reject any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to ≤ 0 at config validation time. The documented disable sentinel (`false`) is unaffected.

**Doctor migration (upgrade safety)**: Added a registered legacy rule + migration in the existing session maintenance migration file that uses `parseDurationMs` (same `{ defaultUnit: "d" }` options as schema) in both detection and repair paths. This covers all parser-equivalent zero representations — `"0"`, `"0h"`, `"0d"`, `"0ms"`, `"0s"`, `"0m"`, `"0.0h"`, `"0h0m"`, `"0h0m0s"`, etc. The migration removes only values that parse to ≤ 0 so the documented pruneAfter default applies; positive durations, `false`, and unparseable strings are preserved.

### Files changed (4 files, +248/-3)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.session.ts` | +14/-3: reject zero-duration in superRefine |
| `src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts` | +27: schema regression cases |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.ts` | +49: parser-backed rule + migration spec |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts` | +155: 16 focused tests |

## Evidence

```
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{
  "valid": false,
  "path": "/tmp/cfg.json5",
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention",
      "message": "duration must be positive (use ms, s, m, h, d), e.g. 30d"
    }
  ]
}
```

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"resetArchiveRetention":"30d"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/cfg.json5","warnings":[]}
```

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"resetArchiveRetention":false}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/cfg.json5","warnings":[]}
```

Doctor detects via parser-backed rule:

```
session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention is a zero duration — this
causes immediate deletion of all reset transcript archives. Run
"openclaw doctor --fix" to remove it so the documented pruneAfter
default applies.
```

Doctor repairs:

```
Removed session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention "0h" (zero duration);
documented pruneAfter default applies.
```

### Unparseable values preserved for schema diagnostic

`"abc"`, `""` — not matched by doctor rule, not removed by migration. Schema diagnostic handles these.

target.title: fix(signal): align supported message actions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal's message-action adapter advertised support for every non-`send` action, but its handler only implements `react`. That meant unsupported actions like `delete` or `pin` could pass the ownership-boundary support check and then fail later inside the handler.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Signal adapter should advertise only the actions it can actually handle. `send` still stays on the normal outbound path, and reaction add/remove behavior remains represented by the existing `react` action parameters.

## User Impact

Unsupported Signal message actions are rejected earlier and consistently by the plugin action support contract. Existing Signal reactions continue to work, and send behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- `extensions/signal/src/message-actions.ts` now returns `true` only for `react` in `supportsAction`.
- `extensions/signal/src/message-actions.test.ts` keeps the existing `send=false` / `react=true` assertions and adds `delete=false` / `pin=false` coverage.
- Current head also registers the real Signal plugin in the shared message-action dispatcher test registry and proves `delete` is declined at the dispatcher boundary while `react` still reaches the Signal reaction handler.

## Proof

- Dispatcher-boundary proof: `dispatchChannelMessageAction({ channel: "signal", action: "delete", ... })` returns `null` for an exact-current Signal conversation and does not call `sendReactionSignal` or `removeReactionSignal`.
- Reaction continuity proof: `dispatchChannelMessageAction({ channel: "signal", action: "react", ... })` returns `{ ok: true, added: "👍" }` and calls `sendReactionSignal("+15550001111", 123, "👍", { accountId: "work", ... })`.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/message-actions.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 8 tests, after rebasing onto remote head `16649e2951`.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/signal/src/message-actions.ts extensions/signal/src/message-actions.test.ts` passed.

- `git diff --check` passed.

target.title: fix(browser): check own profile entries for profile operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser profile names are user-controlled config keys. Inherited object properties such as `constructor` and `prototype` were treated as real profile entries in several create, delete, projection, hot-reload, and gateway patch paths. A valid profile with one of those names could therefore be rejected, omitted, or fail to round-trip.

Live route testing also exposed an adjacent deletion failure: when `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` or `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` placed Browser state outside the OS home/temp roots, deleting a launched profile returned HTTP 500 because the trash helper rejected Browser's own configured state directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Use own-property checks at every Browser profile lookup boundary.
- Preserve valid top-level profile keys while continuing to strip nested prototype-pollution keys from untrusted config patches.
- Keep profile listing and hot reload consistent with persisted config.
- Authorize trash moves only from Browser's owned `<config>/browser` subtree. Existing realpath, symlink-escape, target-identity, and trash-destination checks remain in force; the wider config directory is not authorized.

## User Impact

Profiles named `constructor` or `prototype` can be created, listed, hot-reloaded, patched, and deleted normally. Custom state directories outside the home directory work without granting Browser deletion authority over unrelated config or filesystem paths.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `194d41eab680c1964c70087a60e03df607470878`
- Exact GitHub CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29032054298 - passed.
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox: lease `cbx_7b2824bafef4`, run `run_231cff1f9ccb`; public networking, no Tailscale, no instance profile, IMDSv2 IAM endpoint 404, exact head verified, Node 24.15 / pnpm 11.2.2; 180 focused tests passed. Lease released.
- Native `OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1 scripts/pr prepare-run 101694` - passed at the exact PR head.
- Fresh autoreview at the exact head - clean, confidence 0.91.
- Real Express route proof: create and delete `constructor` through `POST /profiles/create` and `DELETE /profiles/constructor`; persistence round-tripped and `Object.prototype` remained unchanged.
- Real Gateway RPC proof: `config.patch` created and removed the profile while nested `constructor` / `prototype` payload keys remained stripped.
- Custom-state route proof: launched/stopped profile deletion under a configured state directory outside home/temp succeeds; unrelated config subtrees, root config authority, and symlink escapes remain rejected.

Live Dev Gateway + OpenAI agent + Browser proof will be added before merge; it is intentionally not claimed by the current evidence.

target.title: fix(google-meet): guard node-host meet URLs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Google Meet chrome node-host command accepted any non-empty `start.url` before launching Chrome or starting realtime bridge processes. The higher-level node invoke policy already normalizes Meet URLs, but the node-host command is its own execution boundary and direct calls could still pass non-Meet URLs into local Chrome/bridge side effects.

## Why This Change Was Made

This moves the existing Google Meet URL contract into a lightweight shared helper and applies it inside `startChrome` before any BlackHole check, audio bridge startup, or Chrome launch. `runtime.ts` continues to re-export `normalizeMeetUrl`, while `node-invoke-policy.ts` imports the same helper directly so the policy and host boundary cannot drift.

## User Impact

Invalid or non-Meet URLs now fail fast with the same stable Google Meet URL errors used by the runtime and node invoke policy. Valid `https://meet.google.com/...` meeting URLs keep the same launch, bridge, list, and stop behavior.

## Evidence

- `extensions/google-meet/src/node-host.ts` now normalizes `params.url` with the shared Meet URL contract before local side effects.
- `extensions/google-meet/node-host.test.ts` covers a non-Meet realtime start request and proves neither `spawnSync` nor child processes are reached.
- `extensions/google-meet/src/runtime.ts` re-exports the helper so existing callers that import from runtime remain compatible.
- Direct node-host proof on current head invoked `handleGoogleMeetNodeHostCommand()` with `action=start`, `mode=realtime`, `launch=true`, and a non-Meet URL. It returned the Meet URL contract error on Linux before any bridge session existed or was created.

## Proof

- Direct node-host transcript:

```text

platform: linux
before list: {"bridges":[]}
error: url must be an explicit https://meet.google.com/... URL
after list: {"bridges":[]}
```

target.title: fix(cron): persist startup catch-up deferrals
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102236. A startup overflow catch-up slot could be persisted to SQLite while its protection marker existed only in memory. Restarting again before that slot fired let maintenance advance the job to its next natural cron slot, silently losing the deferred run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deferral marker now lives on `CronJobState` as `pendingCatchupDeferral`, so the existing `state_json` persistence and rollback paths own the slot and marker together. The process-local Set and its parallel rollback bookkeeping are removed. Maintenance clears the persisted marker when the slot arrives, when no valid deferred slot remains, or when the job is disabled; execution also clears it after an outcome. Existing rows need no migration because an absent field means no pending deferral.

## User Impact

Overflow system-event cron jobs keep their staggered startup catch-up run across repeated gateway restarts instead of silently skipping to the next natural schedule. Unrelated stale future cron slots are still repaired normally.

## Evidence

- Real SQLite restart path: one service starts and persists an overflow deferral, a fresh service starts 3 seconds later against the same store, the original 5-second slot survives, executes once, and clears its marker.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.startup-overflow-clobber.test.ts src/cron/service.jobs.test.ts src/cron/service/ops.test.ts`: 3 files, 107 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.restart-catchup.test.ts src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts`: 2 files, 81 tests passed.
- Oxlint passed for all nine changed files.

target.title: fix(feishu): bound stalled docx image URL reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users rendering or uploading Feishu docx images from remote URLs could have the docx workflow hang when the remote image response body stalled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Docx image URL reads now go through a Feishu-local remote image reader that applies the selected account's Feishu HTTP timeout as two targeted deadlines: a response-header deadline and a response-body idle deadline. It no longer uses the setting as a complete-operation download deadline, so healthy large image transfers that keep making progress are not cut off solely because total elapsed time exceeds the header timeout. File upload remote reads keep their existing behavior, so this stays scoped to docx image handling.

## User Impact

Feishu docx image processing now degrades through the existing error handling instead of blocking the whole document operation on a stalled remote image body. Account-specific Feishu timeout settings are honored for docx image response headers and stalled body reads without changing the Feishu config schema.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/docx.test.ts` passed: 20 tests.

Fixes an issue where Workboard claim authorization compared claim tokens with ordinary string equality. Claim tokens are redacted credentials that let a worker other than the recorded owner heartbeat, release, or mutate a claimed card, so their validation should use the same timing-safe primitive as other OpenClaw secret-bearing authorization surfaces.

## Why This Change Was Made

## User Impact

Workboard claim authorization now avoids data-dependent string comparison timing for claim tokens. Existing valid and invalid token behavior, error messages, and card workflows remain unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users starting a realtime WebRTC voice session could remain stuck waiting when the SDP offer request returned headers but the answer body stalled.

The WebRTC offer fetch now uses an explicit 30s AbortController deadline that stays active until the SDP answer body has been read. The change keeps the existing setup cancellation and failure flow intact and limits the timeout to the WebRTC offer exchange.

## User Impact

target.title: [Bug]: embedded prompt cache breaks across room-event, policy, and Responses boundaries
target.body:
## Summary

Long-lived embedded sessions can lose provider prompt-cache reuse when adjacent turns cross room-event delivery, authorization, queue, compaction, recovery, or native Responses continuation boundaries.

Sanitized same-session traces showed model-visible tool inventory changing between 44 and 47 tools, prompt/tool digests changing with it, and cached prefixes collapsing to roughly 2k-10k tokens or plateauing around 37k-40k.

After stabilizing request shape, numeric-only records from a long-lived room session show the cached prefix growing from 104,960 to 157,184 tokens; the final four turns reused 98.7-99.2% of the input prefix. Exact-head isolated live-provider probes then reused 40,960 cached tokens on warm GPT-5.5 turns (99.5%) and 40,448 on warm GPT-5.6 turns (98.2-98.3%), with one stable 48-tool ordered shape digest. No transcript text or private identifiers are included.

## Root Cause

Three independent concerns were coupled:

1. turn-specific delivery and authorization changed reusable prompt/tool definitions;
2. reconstructed queue, memory, compaction, fallback, and recovery runs could lose authoritative state;
3. built-in authenticated OpenAI Responses streams could miss native `previous_response_id` continuation.

## Expected Contract

- One stable model-visible prompt and ordered tool catalogue for a session.
- One deterministic, trusted current-turn `ToolAccessPolicy` enforced before side effects.
- Trusted-internal capability remains distinct from owner identity, so limited core-tool grants cannot expose owner-only plugin tools.
- Actual reply routing remains turn-specific without changing prompt-facing tool shape.
- Queue, memory, compaction, provider, and recovery boundaries preserve the same state.
- Authenticated GPT-5.5/GPT-5.6 Responses use native continuation; custom streams retain their routing.
- Supervised Codex turns keep native model/effort/personality settings while receiving trusted turn guidance through append-only developer history.

## Candidate Fix

PR #102189 at `b0a9bfc589f8deff1ed9dd5345276093d6df25b2` implements the contract above.

The candidate includes upstream `7027d2c227281d814266311bebab7581b899d6dc` and has a clean merge-tree check against it. Pre-refresh broad validation passed 2,446 changed-file tests plus focused trusted-internal ownership, compaction, overflow recovery, harness selection, and manual propagation coverage. Exact-head validation passes 14 proof assertions across 18 suites, 215 Codex lifecycle/binding/login-profile tests, production typecheck, prompt snapshots, diff checks, and a full build.

An exact-head focused proof run passes 14 selected assertions across 18 suites: strict room-event delivery, pre-hook/pre-side-effect denial, permitted trusted-internal execution, and GPT-5.5/GPT-5.6 `previous_response_id` delta continuation.

The exact commit is installed on the reporter's local gateway: OpenClaw `2026.7.2`, LaunchAgent loaded, runtime active, connectivity probe OK, dashboard HTTP 200, Discord probe OK, WhatsApp linked/healthy, and build-info commit matches the candidate.

## Privacy

Evidence is intentionally sanitized. No private sender, channel, account, host, endpoint, credential, or raw trace identifiers are included.

Disclaimer: This issue was filed and updated autonomously by Codex on behalf of the reporter.

target.title: fix(fal): apply request policy to media generation requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users configuring FAL provider request policy for media generation would not have that policy applied to FAL image generation HTTP requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

FAL HTTP config now passes `models.providers.fal.request` into the existing provider HTTP request-policy resolver. This keeps FAL on the shared provider request seam and does not change model parameters, generation parsing, or generated image parsing. Explicit private-network opt-in is now honored from the configured request policy instead of being overridden by a hard-coded deny, while the default remains deny.

## User Impact

FAL media generation requests can now honor configured request headers, proxy/TLS transport settings, and explicit private-network request policy through the existing provider request policy mechanism.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/fal/image-generation-provider.test.ts` passed: 44 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/fal/http-config.ts extensions/fal/image-generation-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/fal/http-config.ts extensions/fal/image-generation-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Resolver proof: `resolveFalHttpRequestConfig` with configured `baseUrl`, `request.headers.X-Fal-Trace`, and `request.allowPrivateNetwork: true` returned `allowPrivateNetwork: true` plus the configured header and redacted Authorization header.
- Controlled real provider-path proof, using `buildFalImageGenerationProvider().generateImage()` against a local HTTP server through the normal Fal provider path:

```text
$ FAL_API_KEY=<redacted> node_modules/.bin/tsx --eval '<local Fal-compatible HTTP server + buildFalImageGenerationProvider().generateImage(...) harness>'
{
  "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:<redacted>",
  "requests": [
    {
      "method": "POST",
      "url": "/fal-ai/flux/dev",
      "authorization": "<redacted>",
      "trace": "trace-harness",
      "contentType": "application/json",
      "body": "{\"prompt\":\"draw a local cat\",\"num_images\":1,\"output_format\":\"png\"}"
    },
    {
      "method": "GET",
      "url": "/files/generated.png",
      "body": ""
    }
  ],
  "images": [
    {
      "mimeType": "image/png",
      "fileName": "image-1.png",
      "bytes": 8
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "prompt": "local cat"
  }
}
```

- Not run: live FAL API call.

AI-assisted change.

target.title: feat: MCP Apps (ui://) Phase 0 — generic host in Control UI + plugin-declared MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

Phase 0 of MCP Apps support (the `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` extension implemented by Claude and ChatGPT): OpenClaw's bundle MCP client detects tools that declare interactive `ui://` resources on **any configured MCP server**, fetches the app document after the tool call, and the Control UI renders it in a sandboxed iframe with a minimal MCP Apps postMessage host. Plugins can attach MCP App servers declaratively via a new `mcpServers` manifest field for native plugins.

No server-specific integration is bundled. The official [Excalidraw MCP App server](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw-mcp) served as the proof of concept and lives out of tree as an external plugin ([fuller-stack-dev/openclaw-excalidraw-plugin](https://github.com/fuller-stack-dev/openclaw-excalidraw-plugin)); any spec-conforming server works via `mcp.servers.<name>` config or the plugin manifest field.

**Draft because of one known blocker** (found by Codex review, confirmed empirically): `about:srcdoc` iframes inherit the embedding page's CSP, and the gateway-served Control UI ships `script-src 'self'` (`src/gateway/control-ui-csp.ts`), which blocks inline app scripts before they can initialize. The inline preview therefore only functions on CSP-less deployments (e.g. dev servers) today. The fix — serving app documents from a dedicated ticketed route with per-app CSP headers (the spec's sandbox-proxy pattern) — is the planned Phase 1 host work; this module's bridge, sizing, registry, and all server-side plumbing carry over unchanged. Everything else in the PR (capability negotiation, `_meta.ui` parsing, visibility enforcement, resource fetch, plugin-declared MCP servers, text fallback) works on production deployments now.

## What's in here

**Server side (`src/agents`)**
- Bundle MCP client declares `capabilities.extensions["io.modelcontextprotocol/ui"]` (`mimeTypes: ["text/html;profile=mcp-app"]`).
- `src/agents/mcp-apps.ts`: parses tool `_meta.ui` (nested + deprecated flat `ui/resourceUri` key) and app resources from `resources/read` results (text/blob, CSP + permissions metadata, 5MB cap). All treated as untrusted server output.
- App-only tools (`_meta.ui.visibility` without `"model"`, including explicitly empty lists) never materialize as agent tools.
- After a ui-bearing tool call succeeds, the runtime reads the `ui://` resource and attaches `{ resource, toolInput, result }` as `details.mcpApp` on the tool result. Failures degrade to the plain text result. Tool input is persisted in details because durable transcripts split calls and results into separate messages.

**Control UI (`ui/src`)**
- `details.mcpApp` becomes a `kind: "mcp-app"` tool-card preview rendered in a `sandbox="allow-scripts"` srcdoc iframe (never `allow-same-origin`), with the app-declared CSP inserted structurally via DOMParser and origin expressions validated before interpolation.
- Minimal host bridge: answers `ui/initialize` (protocol `2026-01-26`), pushes `ui/notifications/tool-input` / `tool-result` (incl. `_meta`) after `initialized`, handles `size-changed` and `ping`, and fails fast with JSON-RPC method-not-found for requests Phase 0 does not service (`tools/call`, `ui/open-link`, …) so apps degrade instead of hanging.
- Frames register synchronously via lit `ref()` (srcdoc scripts can post before `load`) and unregister on detach.

**Plugin surface (`src/plugins`)**
- Native (`format: "openclaw"`) plugin manifests can declare `mcpServers` — same shape as `mcp.servers.<name>` config, merged through the existing enabled-bundle path. User config still wins by server name; `enabled: false` detaches a plugin-declared server. Documented in `docs/plugins/manifest.md`.

**Docs**
- Generic MCP Apps behavior/limits section in `docs/cli/mcp.md`; `mcpServers` field in the plugin manifest reference.

## Verification

- Live against `mcp.excalidraw.com` (configured via `mcp.servers`, exercising only the generic path): capability handshake accepted; app-only tools (`export_to_excalidraw`, `save_checkpoint`, `read_checkpoint`) filtered from the materialized tool list; `create_view` produced `details.mcpApp` with the real 432KB `text/html;profile=mcp-app` document and `csp: { connectDomains: ["https://esm.sh"], resourceDomains: ["https://esm.sh"] }`.
- Browser (no-CSP page): the real Excalidraw app booted inside the sandboxed srcdoc iframe under the generated CSP, completed `ui/initialize` → `initialized` → tool-input/tool-result, drew the diagram, and its `size-changed` notifications resized the frame.
- Browser (Control-UI-equivalent CSP header): confirmed the inherited-CSP blocker — iframe mounts, app never boots (hence draft + documented limitation).
- `vitest`: new suites for `_meta.ui`/resource parsing, preview extraction, native-manifest MCP server merge; adjacent suites (tool cards, manifest registry, plugin contracts, loader) all green. `tsgo` core/ui/extensions typechecks clean; `pnpm lint` and `oxfmt` clean.

## Review

Three Codex autoreview rounds (`gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) on the branch diff. Fixed across rounds: frame-registration race ahead of srcdoc execution, `visibility: []` model-exposure bypass, lost tool input on transcript reload, CSP origin-expression injection, regex head-insertion bypass (now DOMParser), `base-uri` honoring `baseUriDomains`, `_meta` passthrough, and detached-frame retention. Escalated rather than patched: the srcdoc CSP-inheritance blocker above (architecture change → Phase 1) and app-initiated `tools/call` proxying (deliberately out of Phase 0 scope; documented as view-only).

Note: `docs/plugins/reference/anthropic.md` is stale against the inventory generator on current `main` (pre-existing; `node scripts/generate-plugin-inventory-doc.mjs --check` fails on a clean checkout). Not touched here.

target.title: fix(config): reject zero-value pruneAfter to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Configuring `session.maintenance.pruneAfter: "0h"` (or any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to zero) is silently accepted by Zod config validation. `parseDurationMs("0h")` returns `0` without throwing, so the `superRefine` passes the value. `resolvePruneAfterMs` returns `0ms` with no guard, and `pruneStaleEntries` computes `cutoff = now - 0 = now`, matching all sessions for immediate deletion.

## Changes

**Schema gate (prevention)**: Added `ms <= 0` guard in `superRefine` to reject any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to ≤ 0 at config validation time.

**Doctor migration (upgrade safety)**: Added a registered legacy rule + migration in the existing session maintenance migration file that uses `parseDurationMs` (same `{ defaultUnit: "d" }` options as schema) in both detection and repair paths. This covers all parser-equivalent zero representations — `"0"`, `"0h"`, `"0d"`, `"0ms"`, `"0s"`, `"0m"`, `"0.0h"`, `"0h0m"`, `"0h0m0s"`, etc. The migration removes only values that parse to ≤ 0 so the documented 30d default applies; positive durations and unparseable strings are preserved.

### Files changed (4 files, +198/-1)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.session.ts` | +14/-3: reject zero-duration in superRefine |
| `src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts` | +17: schema regression cases |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.ts` | +49: parser-backed rule + migration spec |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts` | +118: 14 focused tests |

## Evidence

### All tests passing

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/zod-schema.session-maintenance-extensions.test.ts
Tests  12 passed (12)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.session.test.ts
Tests  14 passed (14)
```

### Before fix: schema gate rejects zero values

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"pruneAfter":"0h"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{
  "valid": false,
  "path": "/tmp/cfg.json5",
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "session.maintenance.pruneAfter",
      "message": "duration must be positive (use ms, s, m, h, d), e.g. 30d"
    }
  ]
}
```

### After fix: positive intervals still accepted

```
$ echo '{"session":{"maintenance":{"pruneAfter":"30d"}}}' > /tmp/cfg.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/cfg.json5","warnings":[]}
```

### Doctor detection → repair

Doctor detects via parser-backed rule:

```
session.maintenance.pruneAfter is a zero duration — this causes
immediate deletion of all sessions. Run "openclaw doctor --fix" to
remove it so the documented 30d default applies.
```

Doctor repairs:

```
Removed session.maintenance.pruneAfter "0h" (zero duration);
documented 30d default applies.
```

### Unparseable values preserved for schema diagnostic

`"abc"`, `""` — not matched by doctor rule, not removed by migration. Schema diagnostic handles these.

### Diff whitespace checks

`git diff --check` passed.

- **Not tested / proof gaps**: None.

target.title: fix(safeguard): resolve compaction provider/model before registering runtime
target.body:
Fixes #57901.

## What Problem This Solves

Normal safeguard auto-compaction still registers the active session model even when `agents.defaults.compaction.model` selects a different summarization target. Main's new route-aware auth planner fixed explicit compaction, but normal safeguard registration still ignored the override.

A safeguard override also needs its model route and credential to remain one atomic tuple. Binding a target credential into the active attempt registry can corrupt same-provider sessions before compaction starts.

## Summary

This refresh is merged with main at `266d49cddb977c45d40f13d27045214db29bc756` and adapts the safeguard override to the current route-aware runtime planner.

- Resolve the configured safeguard target before synchronous extension registration.
- Reuse an existing prepared auth plan only when it exactly matches the target provider/model.
- Otherwise prepare the target through the atomic runtime flow:
  `prepareAgentRuntimeAuth` → `materializePreparedRuntimeModel` → `resolvePreparedRuntimeAuthAttempts` → `resolvePreparedRuntimeModelAuth`.
- Preserve the selected model route, auth requirement, request transport overrides, runtime policy, selected profile, and credential as one tuple.
- Resolve the target with an isolated `AuthStorage`/`ModelRegistry`; never mutate the active attempt's auth registry.
- Carry the prepared model, target registry, and resolved auth plan through the safeguard runtime registry.
- Prefer the prepared safeguard model and its paired registry in the hook.
- Reject prepared routes whose runtime policy does not support the OpenClaw runtime.
- Preserve locked native-harness sessions on their pinned model.
- Warn and fall back to the active model when the configured target cannot be resolved or authenticated.
- Keep explicit compaction on main's current prepared-route implementation while forwarding its resolved model, registry, and auth plan into safeguard runtime state.

## Safety Invariants

- A same-provider override using a different profile cannot replace the active session key.
- Cross-provider model, API, base URL, route requirement, transport overrides, runtime policy, selected profile, and key are resolved together.
- The safeguard hook looks up target credentials in the target registry, not the active attempt registry.
- `buildEmbeddedExtensionFactories` remains synchronous by receiving a precomputed target.

## Evidence

Validated on exact local tree `b38eded0065419c75b3b1f369b96d7359c0cb239`:

- PR head: `9f2ac5d5ac9e17d20e9ec7be684f82157b4b3327`
- Merge parents: prior PR head `ecfc4491ece04b29ccb48c42ecb6a40d6e0d8a37` and main `266d49cddb977c45d40f13d27045214db29bc756`
- Diff from merged main: 9 files, +1022/-21
- Core production TypeScript — passed
- Core test TypeScript — passed
- Planner/safeguard focused suites — 238 tests passed
- Compaction context/resource-loader suites — 62 tests passed
- Duplicate extension-project coverage — 26 tests passed
- Concrete OpenAI route regression asserts API, base URL, auth requirement, request overrides, runtime policy, selected profile, and key
- Same-provider alternate-profile regression proves target-key isolation from the active registry
- `oxfmt --check`, type-aware `oxlint --deny-warnings`, and `git diff --check` — passed
- Independent semantic review confirmed the adapted diff preserves main's atomic route/auth contract

A direct compact-hooks subset currently reproduces 9/102 failures on an unmodified `266d49c` worktree as well as the merge tree; the conflicted compact implementation and harness are byte-identical to main. No unrelated main fix is included here. Fresh exact-head GitHub CI is running.

## Testing Scope

No live provider API call was made. Exact-head automated coverage proves route/auth tuple integrity and active-registry isolation. A real provider-backed automatic cross-provider safeguard compaction remains an external maintainer/environment proof gate.

target.title: Propagate AbortSignal through bundle MCP tool/resource/prompt calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent run is cancelled, pending bundle MCP tool/resource/prompt requests keep running because the per-call `AbortSignal` is dropped after `AgentTool.execute`. This leaves MCP child work alive after the caller has aborted, wastes resources, and can produce late results that race with cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #104110 fixed the same issue for bundle LSP JSON-RPC requests by forwarding the `AbortSignal` and emitting `$/cancelRequest`. Bundle MCP uses the same `AgentTool.execute` contract but ignores the signal all the way down to the MCP SDK client. This change plumbs the signal through the same layers so MCP requests can be cancelled.

## User Impact

- Cancelling an agent turn or session now stops pending bundle MCP tool calls, resource reads, and prompt fetches instead of letting them run to completion.
- Reduces wasted compute and prevents late MCP responses from being applied after cancellation.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test in `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-tools.materialize.test.ts` that verifies the `AbortSignal` is forwarded from each projected tool's `execute` into `runtime.callTool`, `listResources`, `readResource`, `listPrompts`, and `getPrompt`.
- Existing tests pass:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-tools.materialize.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts` → 57 tests passed across 2 shards.
  - `npx oxfmt --check src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-types.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-tools.materialize.test.ts` → clean.
  - `npx oxlint src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-types.ts` → clean.
- Minimal scope: only touches bundle MCP runtime/types/materialize + one focused test file.

target.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.tts.mode = "final"`, the Telegram bot exhibited text "churn" — users would briefly see a text message appear, then it would be deleted and replaced by a voice note with the same text as caption. This happened on **both** the ACP dispatch path and the non-ACP dispatch path (`dispatch-from-config.ts`).

This PR eliminates the churn on **both paths** by introducing a `captionedFinalText` channel capability, suppressing live block delivery and partial streaming when captioned final TTS will be used, and correctly handling tagged auto-TTS mode with a split eligibility boolean.

## Root cause

```
Before (main):
  1. Block text / partial streaming delivers text to user immediately
  2. TTS synthesis runs (2-5 seconds)
  3. Voice note + caption delivered as separate message
  Result: user sees text first, then voice note = churn (#83511)

After (this PR):
  1. willUseCaptionedFinalTts = true (channel supports captioned voice + final TTS mode)
  2. Partial streaming suppressed, block text delivery suppressed
  3. TTS synthesis runs, text accumulated silently
  4. Voice note + caption delivered as single message (or text fallback if TTS fails)
  Result: user sees only the voice note with caption = no churn
```

### Tagged auto-TTS mode

When `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"`, TTS only fires for replies containing `[[tts:...]]` directives. Three additional issues were discovered and fixed:

1. **Split boolean**: `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` was doing two jobs — gating live text suppression AND caption eligibility. Split into `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` (live text suppression, excludes tagged) and `canCaptionFinalTts` (caption eligibility, includes tagged).

2. **Block TTS gate**: The accumulated block TTS fallback was gated on `replies.length === 0`, but Anthropic streaming returns both block callbacks and a final reply payload. Changed to gate on `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` and `queuedFinal` instead.

3. **Partial streaming leak**: `onPartialReply` was active for tagged mode, sending raw `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` directive text to Telegram during streaming, creating a duplicate text message before the voice+caption arrived. Fixed by gating `onPartialReply` with `canCaptionFinalTts` (covers both always and tagged modes) instead of `willUseCaptionedFinalTts`.

### Media block preservation

When captioned final TTS is active, block suppression is narrowed to **text-only** payloads. Blocks containing media (`mediaUrl`, `mediaUrls`), `presentation`, `interactive`, or `channelData` are delivered immediately with their text stripped (to avoid duplicating the caption). This applies to both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` + `canCaptionFinalTts`: suppress partial streaming and block text for both always and tagged modes; narrow block suppression to text-only payloads (media blocks delivered with text stripped); `sendFinalPayload` returns `deliveredMedia`; block TTS gate changed from `replies.length === 0` to `!deliveredFinalTtsMedia && !queuedFinal` |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | Regression tests: tagged directive-only voice+caption, tagged+always both-block-and-final delivery, partial suppression for tagged TTS on caption-capable channels, plain tagged block delivery, media block delivery with text stripped, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` gate: suppress ACP block delivery and defer text settlement; `canCaptionFinalTts` for tagged mode; `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` tracking |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts` | `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` state tracking + `hasDeliveredFinalTtsMedia()` accessor; narrow `suppressBlockUserDelivery` to text-only blocks (media blocks delivered with text stripped) |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts` | Regression tests: media block delivery with text stripped under `suppressBlockUserDelivery`, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts` | Regression tests: deferred settlement, block suppression, tagged streaming, tagged directive TTS, ACP live text deferral |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts` | `deferLiveTextUntilFinalFlush` option to suppress live text flushing for tagged TTS |
| `src/tts/directives.ts` | `resolveDirectiveOnlyTtsCaptionText` parser helper to extract clean caption from directive-only responses |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.ts` | `captionedFinalText: true` capability declaration |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts` | Test for capability declaration |
| `src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts` | JSDoc for `captionedFinalText` capability contract |
| `src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts` | Capability seam test |
| `docs/tools/tts.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability: opt-in criteria via `capabilities.tts.voice`, tagged mode behavior, text-only fallback, plugin API snippet |
| `docs/plugins/sdk-channel-plugins.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability in channel plugin SDK guide: opt-in declaration, media block preservation, fallback behavior, tagged mode |
| `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` | Updated SDK API baseline hash |

## Tests

```
$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts
 ✓ 272 passed (272)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts
 ✓ 38 passed (38)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts
 ✓ 67 passed (67)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.reply-dispatch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.final-outcome-counts.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.acp-abort.test.ts
 ✓ 26 passed (26)   # settle-lifecycle paths, no hang

$ npx vitest run extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts
 ✓ 11 passed (11)

$ npx vitest run src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts
 ✓ 1 passed (1)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Telegram TTS final-mode text-before-voice churn on both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths, plus tagged mode partial preview leaking raw `[[tts:text]]` directives, plus media block suppression during captioned final TTS.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout at commit `05b4483a8f`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. Live Telegram bot (`@thomas_fu_bot`) with Microsoft TTS (`zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural`), `messages.tts.mode: "final"`.

- **Failing proof before fix (live Telegram)**:

  ![Before fix — separate text message + voice message (churn)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-before-fix.png)

  User sent "hello" to the Telegram bot. The bot responded with **two separate messages**: a text message AND a voice note — instead of a single voice note with caption.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built and installed from current head: `npm run build && npm pack && npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz`
  2. Registered and restarted Gateway: `openclaw gateway install && openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Tested with `messages.tts.auto: "always"` and `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"` — sent plain messages and directive-bearing messages to `@thomas_fu_bot` on Telegram

- **Evidence after fix**: Always mode (`messages.tts.auto: "always"`) at commit `05b4483a8f`:

  ![Always mode — voice with caption, single message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-always-mode.png)

  Always-mode replies produce a single voice note with caption text. No text churn, no separate text bubble.

- **Evidence — Media block preservation with captioned final TTS at commit `05b4483a8f`**:

  ![Media block preserved — image delivered + voice note with caption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-media-block.png)

  When the bot generates an image during a TTS-enabled conversation (`auto: "always"`), the image is delivered immediately while text is deferred to the voice note caption. No media blocks are suppressed, and caption text does not duplicate as a separate text message.

- **Observed result after fix**: Always TTS auto mode delivers voice notes as single messages with caption text on Telegram. Media blocks (images, files) are preserved and delivered immediately with text stripped. No text flash, no duplicate messages, no media loss.

- **What was not tested**: Other TTS providers (only Microsoft TTS tested live). Group chat TTS (tested in DM only). Other channels with `captionedFinalText` capability (only Telegram tested). Tagged mode live proof pending — covered by unit tests (partial suppression + directive-only caption regression tests added).

## Settle-lifecycle reconciliation (rebased onto current main)

Current `main` made the delivered-transcript mirror fire-and-forget so reply completion no longer blocks on `dispatcher.waitForIdle()`. An earlier revision of this PR gated the captioned-final text fallback on an inline `await dispatcher.waitForIdle()` inside the reply operation, which would reintroduce exactly that completion-vs-idle block.

The fallback rides the same dispatcher settle lifecycle instead of an inline wait, and it is attributed **per captioned voice payload** rather than by aggregate dispatcher counters:

- Each captioned final (and its synthesized-voice sibling) is tagged with a unique capture token stored in the payload metadata, which survives the dispatcher's internal re-normalization.
- Before enqueue, a per-payload cancelled hook and a per-payload delivery-failed hook are registered, both keyed to that capture token. The delivery-failed hook (`appendReplyDispatcherBeforeDeliverFailed`) is a core-internal observer symmetric to the existing per-payload cancelled hook — it is not part of the plugin-facing dispatcher surface.
- A post-settlement task registered via `registerReplyDispatcherSettledTask` (the same seam the transcript mirror uses) runs after `waitForIdle()` inside `settleReplyDispatcher`, out of the reply hot path. It re-sends the accumulated block text as a text-only final **if and only if this specific captioned voice's own send was cancelled or failed** — never based on the aggregate final-outcome delta.

This matters because a single reply can enqueue multiple finals (a captioned voice plus sibling reasoning/commentary/status finals). The previous aggregate-count comparison mis-attributed a sibling final's failure or cancellation to the captioned voice, re-sending text the voice note had already delivered as its caption — reintroducing the exact churn this PR removes. Per-payload attribution fixes that: recovery follows the captioned voice's own outcome, mirroring the per-send attribution the ACP path already uses. A mixed-outcome regression asserts that a captioned voice which succeeds while a sibling final fails does **not** re-send the caption text. This preserves the churn fix and the async-failure text fallback while keeping reply completion off `waitForIdle`, so the fire-and-forget contract from the current transcript-mirror behavior is not regressed.

### Cancelled final delivery (not just failed)

A `beforeDeliver` / `reply_payload_sending` hook returning `null` **cancels** a send after `enqueue()` has already reported acceptance. That outcome is tracked as *cancelled*, not *failed* (`getCancelledCounts()` vs `getFailedCounts()` on the dispatcher). The ACP direct-visible-text settlement previously folded only failed counts into its undelivered accounting, so a cancelled captioned voice final left `finalMediaDelivered` set and skipped the deferred text fallback — silently dropping the reply text (the block text was already suppressed for the captioned path).

The settlement now folds cancelled block/final counts alongside failed counts (`settleDirectVisibleText` in `dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`, via a new `readDispatcherCancelledCounts` reader mirroring the failed reader). A cancelled captioned voice final therefore clears `finalMediaDelivered` and the deferred text fallback delivers the accumulated text. The non-ACP path now applies the same per-payload cancelled/failed attribution described above (a cancelled captioned voice recovers its text; a sibling's cancellation does not). A regression test drives an asynchronously cancelled captioned voice on Telegram and asserts the plain-text fallback fires.

Closes #83511
